concerns.text: FR-011 mandates performing a sensitivity analysis using an independent ground-truth re-labeling protocol. T036/T036a allow the pipeline to complete with a 'data_unavailable' status and a report stating the analysis was skipped. This silently relaxes the requirement to *perform* the validation, violating the constitutional necessity of validating against label noise.

FR-001 explicitly requires loading VulDeePecker (Python), NIST Juliet (C/C++), and BigVul (JS). T011 lists BigVul as primary and NIST Juliet as fallback, but there is no task to ingest VulDeePecker. This drops the Python dataset requirement, failing to satisfy the multi-language scope mandated by the spec.

FR-004 requires embedding similarity to 'known vulnerable patterns' derived from an external code corpus. T019a downloads the NVD CVE feed (metadata/descriptions), and T019c computes similarity against this metadata. This is a semantic weakening; metadata descriptions are not code snippets, so the 'embedding similarity to code patterns' requirement is not met.

FR-007 and SC-005 require logging inference time per sample and total runtime to verify the 6-hour constraint. T013 logs a 'timeout_risk' state and skips samples but lacks a task to aggregate and write the final structured runtime metrics (total time, per-sample times) required for SC-005 verification.

FR-006 and SC-002 require reporting 'Adjusted R²' to determine if the model explains meaningful variance (>0.10). T030 specifies computing both McFadden's and Cox-Snell/Nagelkerke variants but fails to explicitly designate which one is the primary metric for the SC-002 threshold check, creating an untestable success criterion.
